finding.nature_justification: Local checked first: Save method body (lines 197-239) contains multiple ExecuteCommandAsync calls with no using/TransactionScope visible inside the method - this is readable within OrderService.cs alone. Regional applied: to confirm that the Repository pattern provides no implicit transaction guarantee and that UoW attribute must be explicitly applied, cross 1 layer to DI/UoW registration (SqlSugarConfigureExtensions.cs lines 51-54, UnitOfWorkAttribute.cs lines 14,21) - all located via the immediate Service→Repository interface/constructor chain. Not Systemic because evidence stays within Service→Repository/Client immediate boundary; deeper cross-layer (SqlSugar core internals, transaction scope implementation) not needed for the Claim.
finding.claim: OrderService.Save (lines 197-239) performs multiple DB writes without any transaction wrapping: the update branch (lines 226-230) executes 5 separate ExecuteCommandAsync calls in sequence, the insert branch (lines 235-237) executes 3 separate ExecuteCommandAsync calls in sequence, and the method declaration (lines 197-198) carries only [HttpPost] with no [UnitOfWork] attribute

claim_gate.fq2_explanation: Determinant: Claim is bound to OrderService class + Save method + lines 226-237 + state 'no transaction wrapping' - all directly observable.
claim_gate.fq3_explanation: Inter-rater: Two independent agents reading OrderService.cs:197-239 can verify (a) attribute presence at lines 197-198, (b) sequential ExecuteCommandAsync calls at 226-230 and 235-237, (c) absence of using/TransactionScope between them - no semantic ambiguity.
